builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Post-Training Large Language Models with LLMON
summary: The method replaces conventional flat prompting, where instructions and data are indistinguishable to the model, with a post-trained structured format (LLMON) that enforces identifier-based execution semantics. It costs a full post-training pipeline: construction of a 4.6B-token structured corpus with distractor variants, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning on base models, which exceeds a limited cloud budget if replicated at the reported scale. It can fail on instruction formats or injection patterns outside the training distribution, since the defense depends on the model having internalized LLMON semantics rather than on a guaranteed architectural constraint.
rationale: The security gain is substantial and relevant to production RAG and tool-calling systems, but the reported results require a multi-stage post-training effort over billions of tokens, so a small team with one 24 GB GPU should monitor for released checkpoints or distilled variants rather than reproduce the pipeline now.

claims.statement: The method replaces conventional flat prompting, where instructions and data are indistinguishable to the model, with a post-trained structured format (LLMON) that enforces identifier-based execution semantics. It costs a full post-training pipeline: construction of a 4.6B-token structured corpus with distractor variants, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning on base models, which exceeds a limited cloud budget if replicated at the reported scale. It can fail on instruction formats or injection patterns outside the training distribution, since the defense depends on the model having internalized LLMON semantics rather than on a guaranteed architectural constraint.
Reduces attack success rates on indirect prompt-injection benchmarks from 53-100% to 0.02-5.6% on post-trained Granite-4.1 3B and 8B models while preserving general capabilities.
